reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space (a real Hilbert space), with no finite-dimensionality assumption. Let f:E→ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E, and let m be any real number, without a sign restriction. Then the following two global statements are equivalent: (1) for every x,y∈E, m‖y−x‖² ≤ ⟨∇f(y)−∇f(x),y−x⟩; (2) for every x,v∈E, m‖v‖² ≤ D²f(x)[v,v]. The gradient is the Riesz representative of the first Fréchet derivative, and D²f(x)[v,v] means the derivative of the first Fréchet derivative at x applied successively to v and v. The same fixed m is used in both inequalities.
objects: E, f, m, pairs x,y, directions v, the gradient, and the second Fréchet derivative.

quantifiers: Universal over E, f and m satisfying the assumptions; each side of the equivalence has its own universal point/direction quantifiers.
assumptions: f is C² on all E. Completeness and real inner-product structure are global assumptions. No sign assumption on m.
scopes: Regularity and the asserted property hold on the entire displayed space, not merely on a subset or at selected points.
constant_dependencies: m is an arbitrary globally fixed real parameter shared by both statements; there are no existential or dimension-dependent constants.
